text: This is the revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show his servants what must soon happen; he sent it by his angel to John.
John testifies to the word of God and to what Jesus Christ showed him.
A blessing on the one who reads this prophecy aloud and on those who hear and keep it, for the time is near.
John writes to the seven churches in Asia, wishing them grace and peace from God, who is and was and is coming, and from the seven spirits before his throne,
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, first to rise from the dead and ruler of earth's kings. He loves us and freed us from our sins by his blood,
and made us a kingdom and priests for his God and Father. To him be glory and power forever.
He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him; all the tribes of the earth will mourn.
The Lord God says he is the Alpha and the Omega, the one who is and was and is coming, the Almighty.
John, a brother who shares the suffering, kingdom and patient endurance in Jesus, was on the island of Patmos because of God's word.
On the Lord's day he was in the Spirit and heard behind him a loud voice like a trumpet,
telling him to write what he sees and send it to the seven churches: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea.
He turned to see the voice and saw seven golden lampstands,
and among them one like a son of man, dressed in a long robe with a golden sash.
His head and hair were white like wool and snow, his eyes like blazing fire,
his feet like bronze glowing in a furnace, and his voice like the sound of many waters.
In his right hand were seven stars, from his mouth came a sharp double-edged sword, and his face shone like the sun at full strength.
When John saw him he fell at his feet as though dead. He laid his right hand on John and said not to be afraid: he is the first and the last,
the living one who died and is alive forever, and holds the keys of Death and Hades.
So John is to write what he has seen, what is now, and what will happen later.
The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.
